evals.name: Static site with defaults
evals.description: URL given, everything else default. Tests the happy path: ask only what is missing, the filename convention, A4, and platform-appropriate delivery.
evals.prompt: Please save this documentation site into one document: https://help.example.com/getting-started
assertions: At most the format, depth, and domain-scope defaults (Word, unlimited, same domain only) are confirmed — the URL is never asked for again
The filename follows {domain}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{depth_label}.{ext}, e.g. help_example_com_[date]_full.docx
The Word file is A4
On Claude Code the absolute file path is reported; on claude.ai the platform's file delivery presents the file in the conversation
The document contains a cover page, a table of contents, one section per page with source URL, and a References and Attachments section when binary files are linked

A link that answers with something other than a web page (a full-size image, a JSON endpoint) is skipped on its headers, without its body being downloaded and thrown away, and the skip counts as neither a page nor an error

evals.name: JavaScript-rendered site
evals.description: SPA detected at analysis. Tests the JS branch: connector used when present, honest failure when absent, and the sparse-content stop on the pipeline path.
evals.prompt: Convert https://app.example.com/docs into a Word document.
assertions: JavaScript rendering is detected in the analysis step and the user is told before extraction starts
If a Chrome MCP connector is available, the skill switches to the Chrome MCP workflow instead of static fetching, using the connector's actual tool names
If no connector is available, the skill says plainly that full extraction is not possible in this environment, offers best-effort static extraction, and does not claim success

On the Claude Code pipeline, a run ending in SPARSE CONTENT WARNING builds no document: the extracted pages are saved to pages.json and the user is offered re-extraction via Chrome MCP or a best-effort rebuild from that file

On a site the analysis called JavaScript-rendered, the pipeline gives up after its first ten near-empty pages rather than crawling the whole site first; a static site whose landing pages happen to be thin still runs to completion

evals.name: Configuration pre-answered (PDF, 2 levels, subdomains)
evals.description: Format, depth, and scope all stated in the request. Tests ask-only-what-is-unanswered and the Nlevels filename label.
evals.prompt: Archive learn.example.com as PDF, 2 levels deep, following subdomains too. Don't ask me anything else.
assertions: No configuration question is asked: format, depth, and scope were all stated in the request
The filename carries the 2levels label, e.g. learn_example_com_[date]_2levels.pdf
Links are followed only on the base domain and its subdomains
The PDF is A4 and contains a table of contents

evals.name: robots.txt and binary links
evals.description: Extraction of a site that disallows some paths, asks for a crawl delay, and links binary files. Tests robots compliance and the References-and-Attachments contract.
evals.prompt: Please extract everything from https://help.example.com into Markdown, including any files it links to.
assertions: robots.txt is respected: disallowed pages are skipped and logged
Binary files (PDF, ZIP, etc.) are not fetched; they are listed in the References and Attachments section of the document
Blocked or unreachable domains are excluded automatically and reported in the final summary
Per-page errors are logged and the extraction continues rather than aborting

A Crawl-delay in robots.txt is respected: the crawl is paced at the interval the site asks for, the user is told the pace before extraction starts, and a lower --rate-limit does not override it; on a branch that cannot wait between fetches the user is told the site asks for an interval this environment cannot honour, instead of the crawl going ahead at full speed

evals.name: Same site extracted twice
evals.description: A repeat extraction that would repeat the filename. Tests the never-overwrite collision rule, now enforced by the Claude Code script as well.
evals.prompt: Extract https://help.example.com into Word, full depth. This exact extraction already ran earlier today — the archive file named for today, help_example_com_<today>_full.docx, is already in the working directory. Do not lose it.
assertions: Before writing, the skill checks whether the target filename already exists and applies the _v2 (then _v3) collision rule instead of silently overwriting
Any pre-existing archive is preserved byte-for-byte, and the user is told exactly which file was created

evals.name: Italian conversation, English scaffold
evals.description: The user writes in Italian. Tests the three language layers: Italian conversation, English scaffold labels, untranslated site content.
evals.prompt: Trasforma il sito https://assistenza.example.com in un documento Word, per favore.
assertions: The conversation is in Italian, including any questions and the final summary
The document's fixed scaffold labels (cover, Table of Contents, References) are English
The site's own content is reproduced in its original language, never translated

evals.name: Chrome MCP bookkeeping loop
evals.description: JavaScript site extracted through the Chrome MCP workflow on Claude Code. Tests per-page saving with chrome_extract.py, dedup, image embedding, and the pages-file build.
evals.prompt: Use the Chrome MCP connector to archive https://app.example.com/docs into a Word document.
assertions: Each visited page is saved through chrome_extract.py with --html-file and --pages-file, one call per page, and the same literal pages-file path in every call
A URL already saved is skipped by the script's dedup, not saved twice
Images in the rendered pages are downloaded and embedded in the built document, not left as placeholders
The final document is built with main.py --pages-file from the collected pages, not by re-scraping
The output filename follows {domain}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{depth_label}.{ext} and never overwrites an existing file
On a page declaring <base href>, relative links and image addresses resolve against that base, not against the page's own address

evals.name: Subdomain scope on a two-level country domain
evals.description: A site on a two-level country ending (help.example.co.uk) crawled with subdomain scope. Tests that the scope expands to the registrable domain only, not to every site sharing the country ending.
evals.prompt: Archive https://help.example.co.uk as Markdown, following subdomains too.
assertions: Links are followed on help.example.co.uk, example.co.uk, and other subdomains of example.co.uk only
An unrelated site sharing only the country ending (other-site.co.uk) is excluded from the crawl
The filename follows {domain}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{depth_label}.{ext}, e.g. help_example_co_uk_[date]_full.md

evals.name: Bare domain start URL
evals.description: The crawl starts from a bare domain with no path. Tests that the homepage is archived exactly once, not once per URL spelling.
evals.prompt: Archive https://example.com as Markdown, full depth.
assertions: The homepage appears exactly once in the document — the bare-domain URL and the trailing-slash URL are treated as the same page
A self-link spelled https://example.com/index.html is the same visited page as the homepage: directory-index spellings fold to the directory URL
The filename follows {domain}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{depth_label}.{ext}, e.g. example_com_[date]_full.md

evals.name: Depth-limited run on a site with a sitemap
evals.description: The site publishes a sitemap.xml listing many pages, but the user asks for 2 levels. Tests that a depth limit means link hops and the sitemap informs the estimate, not the crawl.
evals.prompt: Archive https://docs.example.com as Word, 2 levels deep only.
assertions: The Step 2 estimate uses the sitemap page count, and the user is told the site is large if it is
The crawl follows links only (site navigation included): sitemap URLs are not seeded when a depth limit is set
Pages within 2 link hops of the start URL are included; pages reachable only through the sitemap are not
The filename carries the 2levels label, e.g. docs_example_com_[date]_2levels.docx

The depth-limited build run reads no sitemap at all: the count comes from the separate analysis run, and Phase 1 of the build says the sitemap was not read rather than spending hundreds of paced fetches on a list the crawl cannot use

evals.name: Site with unwrapped text content
evals.description: A site that puts text directly in divs and spans, uses definition lists, and adds figure captions — no p wrappers. Tests that bare text is captured, not silently dropped.
evals.prompt: Please convert https://campaign.example.com into one Word document.
assertions: Text placed directly in divs and spans (no p wrapper) appears in the document as paragraphs, in document order
Definition-list terms and definitions, and figure captions, appear in the document
Navigation and menu text does not appear as content
No content-bearing text is dropped without the sparse-content warning path being taken (the page is not sparse — the extractor captured it)
Markup inside a <template> element, which no browser renders, does not reach the document — while a panel that merely starts hidden, as an accordion or a tab does, keeps its content

evals.name: Mixed apex and www internal links
evals.description: A site whose internal links mix example.com and www.example.com spellings. Tests www folding in same-domain scope and in the visited set.
evals.prompt: Archive https://example.com as Word, full depth, same domain only.
assertions: Pages linked through both host spellings (example.com and www.example.com) are included in the crawl
No page appears twice: the apex and www spellings of the same path are one visited page
Other domains linked from the site stay excluded (same-domain scope)
A link whose fetch redirects to a host outside the agreed scope is skipped, not archived at the address it landed on

evals.name: Nested lists and multi-paragraph list items
evals.description: A documentation page with lists inside lists, and list items holding more than one paragraph. Tests that nesting survives into the document and that no words are joined together.
evals.prompt: Convert https://docs.example.com/guide into a Word document.
assertions: A list nested inside another list is indented in the output, not flattened to the same level as its parent
An ordered list interrupted by a sublist keeps counting: the item after the sublist is 2, not 1 again
Words on either side of a nested block are separated: an item reading 'Parent' followed by a sublist never comes out as 'Parentalpha'
A list item containing two paragraphs reads as two separated phrases, not one glued word
A paragraph written across several source lines appears as one line of text, without the line breaks the HTML source happened to be indented with

evals.name: One linked domain refuses connections
evals.description: A crawl in subdomain scope where one linked host is unreachable. Tests that the domain is excluded once, does not consume the error budget, and is recorded in the archive.
evals.prompt: Archive https://help.example.com as Word, following subdomains too.
assertions: The unreachable domain is reported once, not once per URL on it, and no further requests are sent to it
The failures on that domain do not count toward the ten-consecutive-error stop: the crawl of the reachable pages finishes normally
The unreachable domain is named in the document's References and Attachments section and in the summary to the user
A page that merely times out is retried as a normal per-page failure and does not exclude its whole domain
Pages that fail with an HTTP status are reported with that status, so a 403 or 429 can be told apart from a 404

evals.name: Site name in the page header, content classes that look like navigation, and headings wrapped in a contents backlink
evals.description:
A documentation site that repeats its own name in an

inside the page header, whose content sits in classes such as protocol-spec, in-stock, lunch-menu and navigation-api-reference, and whose section headings are written by docutils as

…

. Tests that section titles stay distinct per page, that no content block is mistaken for navigation, and that headings survive.
evals.prompt: Convert https://docs.example.com into one Word document.
assertions: Every page section carries its own title: the site name repeated in the page header does not become the title of all sections
The table of contents lists distinct entries, one per page, not the same name repeated
A page whose only heading is the site logo still gets a title, taken from the page's own <title> element
Content inside classes that merely contain a navigation word as a substring (protocol-spec, in-stock) appears in the document; a real table-of-contents block (page-toc, id=toc) does not

A content block whose class or id merely contains a navigation word (lunch-menu, banner-specs, announcements-archive, navigation-api-reference, id=naval-architecture) appears in the document; a real navigation block (a link-dense sidebar or menu, a breadcrumb, the page header) does not
An article's own <header> keeps its byline and date, while the page-level header is dropped

Section headings written as

Title

appear as headings in the document and in its table of contents, not as missing text

evals.name: Nested tables, lazy-loaded images, and links
evals.description: A product page with a table inside a table, images whose address sits in data-src or srcset, and links in running text. Tests table separation, lazy-image capture, and link preservation per format.
evals.prompt: Convert https://shop.example.com/specs into a Markdown document.
assertions: A table nested inside another table appears as its own table, and the enclosing cell holds only its own text — no inner-table words glued into it, no inner rows repeated
Images whose real address is in data-src, data-original or srcset are downloaded and appear in the document
Bold and inline-code formatting inside table cells is preserved, as it already is in paragraphs and lists
Links in running text are clickable in Markdown and PDF output; in Word the link text appears with no raw [text](url) brackets anywhere
A table whose header row is narrower than its body rows (a colspan header) keeps every body cell in all three formats — no value is dropped to match the header's width
Rebuilding the same crawl into a second format from the collected pages keeps every picture embedded, taken from the image files already on disk, rather than reducing them to [Image: …] placeholders
A row shorter than a cell spanning down into it keeps that cell's value: the merged text appears in every row it covers, and in no row below them

An image address pointing at the machine's own network (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, a name resolving to a private address) is skipped without a request being sent; a site archived from such an address keeps its own images

evals.name: robots.txt across two hosts
evals.description: A subdomain-scope crawl where a second host publishes its own robots.txt. Tests that each host is judged by its own rules and that withheld pages are recorded in the archive.
evals.prompt: Archive https://help.example.com as Word, following subdomains too.
assertions: Each host is checked against its own robots.txt: a path the start host disallows is not assumed disallowed on another host, and a path the second host disallows is skipped
robots.txt is fetched once per host, not once per page
Pages skipped for robots.txt are named in the document's References and Attachments section, not only on the console
A site that publishes several Sitemap: lines in robots.txt has all of them read, not only the last one

evals.name: One section of a large site, with a page cap
evals.description: A big documentation site where the user wants only one branch of it, and the analysis counts more than 200 pages. Tests the Section parameter of Step 1 (path prefixes rather than a guessed depth) and the max-pages question of Step 2.
evals.prompt: Archive only the developer guide from https://docs.example.com — everything under /docs/, but skip the old /docs/legacy/ pages. Markdown is fine.
assertions: The section is expressed as URL path prefixes, not as a guessed depth number: --include-path docs/ and --exclude-path docs/legacy/ on Claude Code, the same prefix rule applied by hand on claude.ai
The prefixes are written without a leading slash, so the command survives Git Bash on Windows
The exclude prefix wins over the include prefix: no page under /docs/legacy/ is archived, while the rest of /docs/ is
The start URL is archived even though it sits outside the include prefix — it is the page the crawl follows links from
When the Step 2 count exceeds 200 pages, the user is asked whether to set a maximum before extraction starts, and the agreed limit is passed as --max-pages
The Step 2 homepage-link count is reported as a figure for the whole site, not for the chosen section: it ignores the path prefixes and so overstates a section run

A section index linked without a trailing slash (/docs) is archived under --include-path docs/, and the excluded branch's index (/docs/legacy) is withheld under --exclude-path docs/legacy/ — the two spellings are one page

evals.name: One page only
evals.description: The user asks for a single page, not a site. Tests that a named page is read as a depth the user gave, not as a missing one that takes the unlimited default.
evals.prompt: Save this page as a Word file: https://docs.example.com/guide/install
assertions: The request is read as depth 0: only the named page is fetched, and no link on it is followed
The unlimited default is not applied — the user is not asked how many levels to follow, and the whole site is not crawled
The filename carries the page depth label, e.g. docs_example_com_[date]_page.docx
The document has one content section, with that page's source URL and breadcrumb

evals.name: JavaScript site on claude.ai — refuse rather than deliver a thin document
evals.description: On claude.ai no script measures the extraction, so the Step 3.5 content check is the model's job. Tests that a site whose pages return almost no text stops the build instead of producing a near-empty archive.
evals.prompt: Archive https://app.example.com into a Word document. (Every page returns a near-empty shell: about 40 characters of text and no pictures.)
assertions: The document is not built: the Step 3.5 content check fails at about 40 characters per page, well under the 150-character bar, with no pictures to compensate
The user is told plainly that static fetching could not extract this site's content
The Chrome MCP workflow is offered as the way to re-extract it properly
No half-empty Word file is delivered, and no file path or download link is invented

evals.name: Right-to-left site content
evals.description: A site written in Arabic or Hebrew. Tests that the site's own text keeps its reading direction in the Word and PDF output while the English scaffold labels stay left-to-right, and that nothing is translated.
evals.prompt: Archive https://docs.example.sa into a Word document.
assertions: The Arabic page text is not translated: the document carries the site's own language
Paragraphs, headings and list items holding Arabic text read right-to-left in the Word file; a right-to-left table has its columns mirrored
The fixed scaffold labels (cover, Table of Contents, References) stay English and left-to-right, because they are the skill's own text and not the site's
The conversation is held in the language of the user's request, not the site's

evals.name: Chrome MCP build on claude.ai reaches the pre-write gate
evals.description: A JavaScript-rendered site extracted through the Chrome MCP connector on claude.ai. Tests that Step E of the browser workflow does not skip Step 3.5: nothing on the --pages-file / conversation-assembly route enforces the checks, so the model applies them itself before building.
evals.prompt: Archive https://app.example.com/docs into a Word document. I am on claude.ai and I have the Chrome MCP connector enabled.
assertions: The site is called JavaScript-rendered and the Chrome MCP workflow is used, not static fetching

Before the document is built, the Step 3.5 checks are applied by the model: content per page, page count against the agreed scope, A4, the filename convention, the References section, and no empty chapter
A page that yielded nothing is listed in the References section rather than written as an empty chapter
If the rendered pages still fall under the content bar, the document is NOT built and the model says which check failed
The model does not claim that a script enforced the checks: on this route nothing does
The file is presented through the platform's file delivery, with no constructed path or download link

eval_notes: 22 prompt-only cases: the input is a site URL, so there is no fixture to upload. They cover parameter collection and the skip rule, the depth and domain-scope options, path filters, the rate limit and the pace robots.txt asks for, robots.txt compliance on every host, HTTP 403 and 429 handling, off-scope redirects, a named single page as a depth the user gave, the JavaScript-rendered and bot-protected branches, the Chrome MCP requirement and its absence, the filename convention with its never-overwrite counter, the Step 3.5 pre-write checks on both branches — including the Chrome MCP route, where nothing enforces them because a --pages-file build checks only the filename counter — and right-to-left site content. Operational only: they grade the conversation and the document, never the pipeline's internals, which `scripts/test_scrape.py` covers instead.
